label: Полный / Пустой
description: Полный vs пустой: full/empty contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Полный' takes the masculine ending to match 'стакан'. The sentence anchors the form in a simple kitchen observation.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Пустая' takes the feminine ending to match 'бутылка'. The everyday context makes the emptiness concrete and easy to picture.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Пустое' takes the neuter ending to match 'ведро'. The spatial phrase shows the learner switching endings in a real scene.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Полные' takes the plural ending to match 'карманы'. The image of full pockets fixes the form in a lively everyday picture.

missions.phrase: Полный автобус ехал мимо пустой остановки.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Direct contrast across two genders. 'Полный' matches masculine 'автобус' while 'пустой' matches feminine 'остановки' in the genitive. The single scene pairs both adjectives in motion.
Strategic focus: Masculine predicate adjective. 'Пустой' stands after the noun as a predicate describing 'холодильник'. The familiar complaint roots the form in daily life.

Strategic focus: Feminine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'была', 'полной' takes the feminine instrumental ending to match 'тарелка'. This shows the common быть-plus-instrumental pattern.

Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'пустыми' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'залы'. The sentence extends the быть-plus-instrumental pattern into the plural.

missions.phrase: Этот ящик полон, а тот пуст.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Short-form masculine contrast. The short forms 'полон' and 'пуст' set the two boxes against each other in a crisp predicate. Short forms are typical when stating a current state.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Полнее' is the comparative of 'полный' and stays unchanged for any gender. The sentence compares two glasses to show degree.
